configuration: Four upstream cases of unittest/com.cpp on the frozen model. Upstream's test_com and test_mass run at an all-ones configuration with the quaternion renormalised, which is a construction rather than a draw and is kept exactly as upstream writes it; the frozen operands supply the configuration and velocity of the subtree-Jacobian case.
observable: the centre of mass, its velocity, acceleration and Jacobian, and the total and subtree masses
default_vs_upstream: upstream, except that one frozen model replaces the random draws
variant: Two units in the last place, toward positive infinity, on nine active initial-condition numbers. Six are operands: one free-flyer orientation coordinate and one joint angle of each frozen configuration (q[3], q[7], q_alt[3], q_alt[7]) and the first velocity coordinate of each (v[0], v_alt[0]). Three are model numbers, because the model is itself an initial-condition input and some graded quantities depend on it alone: the mass and the first lever component of the first body, and the leading rotation entry of the root joint's placement. That set was chosen by measurement, through four corrections. A joint angle alone is erased wherever a case overwrites q.tail(nq-7) before computing. A free-flyer translation alone is inert, rigid-body dynamics being invariant under translation of the floating base. A base orientation alone cannot reach a case that zeroes gravity, which is then invariant under base rotation too, and no operand at all reaches a total mass. No inertial number reaches a Jacobian, which is why the root placement is perturbed as well, that being the one placement premultiplying the whole tree; perturbing its translation was rejected because it is zero and two ulps above zero is a subnormal, and perturbing a mid-tree placement was rejected because it reaches only that joint's descendants. The worst measured spread is 7.1054e-15 absolute. 1 of the 12 observables show a spread of exactly zero and are insensitive by construction, not by accident: subtree_masses. Each is evaluated at a configuration the upstream case constructs rather than draws, or is a mass sum, so it responds only to the perturbed model numbers and not to any operand. Their bound therefore rests on the physical argument in the warrant rather than on a measured sensitivity, and the curator should read it as such.
altbuild: none: the same source built at -O0 with -ffp-contract=off reproduces the -O2 result bit-identically for this module, so an alternative build measures a floor of exactly zero and supplies no evidence. Eigen fixes the evaluation order of these expressions and the recursions are scalar, so the compiler has nothing to reassociate.

evidence.floor_how: The same official.cpp compiled twice against the same pinned source, once at -O2 -DNDEBUG and once at -O0 -ffp-contract=off, and run on ic/nominal; every graded value was bit-identical, so the measured floor is 0.0 and the bound is set from the variant spread and the physics instead.

warrant: The graded quantities are the centre of mass, its velocity and acceleration, its Jacobian and the subtree masses, in SI units and in the model's own degree-of-freedom, joint or Cartesian-axis order, which is fixed by the frozen model rather than chosen by the implementation. The bound is 1e-09 absolute plus 1e-11 relative, so on the largest graded magnitude here, about 2.33e+01, it admits about 1.23e-09. It is physical because every implementation fault this test can express is many orders of magnitude larger: omitting a body from the mass-weighted sum, mis-weighting a subtree, or losing a term of the centre-of-mass Jacobian, each of which moves individual values by between 1e-1 and 1e2 in these units, seven to ten decades above the bound; and the upstream identities, which compare two independent routes to the same quantity, stay active as well, so such a fault is rejected twice over. It is achievable because a correct port that reassociates the recursion differs by about n*eps*|x|, roughly 32 * 2.2e-16 * 1e3, near 7e-12, three decades inside the bound. Measured on this host: the two-ulp variant moves the worst graded value by 7.1054e-15, using 5.761e-06 of the bound, that is 173,584 times of headroom across all 336 graded values, and the alternative build measured exactly zero. The bound is loose enough for a genuinely different implementation on another device and tight enough that no fault the upstream test is written to catch could pass it.
